plan.title: Liver 3' tag-seq DESeq2 treated vs control DE + pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: Three treated vs three control liver samples, single batch, quantified by STAR/featureCounts as raw gene-level counts from a Lexogen QuantSeq 3' tag-seq library (12000 genes x 6 samples). Because the library is 3' tag-based, gene counts do not scale with transcript length, so counts go into DESeq2 unmodified with no length correction and no tximport-style import. The plan follows the grounded procedure: (1) sample-structure QC with a blind VST, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample-distance heatmap to check that treated and control separate and that no sample is an outlier, plus a check that the declared strand protocol is consistent across samples; (2) a minimal low-count pre-filter using a lowered floor (>=5 counts, appropriate for 3' tag-seq per the sourced rule) in at least 3 samples (the smallest group size); (3) an explicit DESeq2 design (~condition, reference level = control) and Wald test, with apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change and BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05; (4) preranked fgsea against MSigDB Hallmark (rank metric = Wald statistic), followed by WikiPathways and GO-BP as secondary collections, since only 6 samples give limited power for a discrete gene-list ORA; (5) a single consolidated report stating the explicit power caveat for n=3/group (low sensitivity, biased toward large effects), fit diagnostics (MA plot, dispersion plot), the reproducibility record (session info, package versions, gene-set collection versions), and the enrichment method-dependence caveat. No batch correction is needed (single batch, unpaired). Reference resources used: MSigDB Hallmark human (2026.1), WikiPathways human (2026.07.10), MSigDB GO-BP human (2026.1), and org.Hs.eg.db for identifier mapping — all confirmed present in the environment.
